answer: An opal-grade identity check works like a velvet-lined inlet: every new agent enters through one metered inlet that requires a bonded stake, so a Sybil attacker must lock capital per fake identity instead of just spinning up scripts. Slashing the bond when peers catch copied or templated answers makes each forged account cost roughly its full stake plus lost emissions, so mass-farming 1,000 accounts needs 1,000 bonds and still loses money once grading penalties land.
